scope.method: static parse of every claim in all 27 wave files; DOI liveness/title match sampled on 31 distinct bare DOIs via Crossref api.crossref.org; web-URL liveness spot-checked with curl

patterns.fix: Normalize at the source in apps/api/scripts/consolidate-research.ts so doi_url is always absolute: after `const raw = (c.citation?.doi_or_url ?? '').trim();` set `const doiUrl = /^10\.\d{4,9}\//.test(raw) ? `https://doi.org/${raw}` : raw;` and use doiUrl for both the dedup key (line 102) and the INSERT (line 142). Zero-padded DOIs (/^10\./) with no scheme would otherwise resolve against the current page as a relative path. Keep the existing SessionDetail.svelte sourceHref() guard as a defence-in-depth fallback.

patterns.note: All five are ISBN strings in the doi_or_url field. sourceHref() returns undefined for them, so they render as unlinked plain text (no crash, but no link).

examples.title: 80/20 Running: Run Stronger and Race Faster by Training Slower

patterns.fix: Either leave the field empty and put the ISBN in a dedicated notes/isbn field, or canonicalize to a resolvable URL: map `ISBN <digits>` to `https://openlibrary.org/isbn/<digits>`. Note the same book is already cited elsewhere as the openlibrary URL (research/wave-3/... uses https://openlibrary.org/isbn/9781450431835), so canonicalizing also merges the duplicate source row.

patterns.note: 21 distinct papers are cited in one file as a bare DOI and in another as https://doi.org/<same DOI>. consolidate-research.ts keys the source id off the RAW doiUrl string (line 102), so each form gets its own research_sources row: the same paper appears twice in the sources list.
patterns.fix: Same normalization as bare-doi-no-url-scheme: compute the id from a normalized key (`doiUrl.toLowerCase()` after stripping any `https://doi.org/` or `doi:` prefix) so both forms collapse to one source row. Alternatively normalize all values to a single canonical form at authoring time.
Upgrade to https:// (the host serves https) or replace with the peer-reviewed source. Other external URLs are https://.

patterns.note: External URLs that resolve but point at product/promotional/facilities pages rather than the cited work. One has an edition mismatch between the URL and the title.

patterns.fix: Prefer a DOI/PubMed/PMC link to the primary work; if a commercial page is intentional, mark citation.type consistently and fix the edition mismatch (make the URL and title describe the same edition).

patterns.note: Normalization was applied per-wave (likely per research agent), not globally: some files are 100% https://doi.org/, others 100% bare DOI. wave-1 66/156 bare, wave-2 94/156 bare, wave-3 41/157 bare, wave-4 48/60 bare. Files at 0 bare: 3a,3b,4a,4b (wave-1); 4a,4b,7b (wave-2); 8a,9a,9b,10a,10b (wave-3).
patterns.fix: Normalize globally in the consolidation step (single source of truth) instead of relying on per-file authoring, so new waves cannot reintroduce the split.

findings.issue: Bare DOIs (no scheme) are stored verbatim into research_sources.doi_url: 249 of 529 claims (47%, 183 distinct papers) across every wave start with '10.' instead of 'https://doi.org/'. The API passes the raw value through (apps/api/src/routes/explanations.ts:62) and the column is indexed as-is (packages/shared/src/db/schema.ts:203). Any consumer that renders doi_url directly as an href would emit a broken relative link. Today's only renderer (SessionDetail.svelte:57) already prefixes https://doi.org/, so live links are NOT broken, but the stored knowledge-base data is non-canonical and unsafe for any new consumer, export, or SQL report.
findings.fix: Normalize in consolidate-research.ts before storing: `const raw = (c.citation?.doi_or_url ?? '').trim(); const doiUrl = /^10\.\d{4,9}\//.test(raw) ? `https://doi.org/${raw}` : raw;` then use doiUrl for the dedup key (line 102) and the INSERT (line 142). Keep SessionDetail.svelte sourceHref() as a fallback.

findings.issue: Five claims put an ISBN (not a DOI or URL) in doi_or_url: 'ISBN 978-0451470881' x3, 'ISBN 0-87322-959-2', 'ISBN 978-1450431835'. These land in the doi_url column and render as unlinked text because sourceHref() only matches ^https?:// or ^10.<4+digits>.
findings.fix: Canonicalize to https://openlibrary.org/isbn/<digits> at consolidation, or keep the ISBN out of doi_url (empty string) and store it elsewhere. The same book is already cited as an openlibrary URL in another file, so canonicalizing also dedupes.

findings.issue: The source id is derived from the raw doi_or_url string, so a paper cited once as '10.x/y' and once as 'https://doi.org/10.x/y' produces TWO research_sources rows. 21 distinct papers have both forms across files (e.g. 10.1249/mss.0b013e31806010e0, 10.1136/bjsports-2020-102955, 10.1007/s40279-023-01978-y). This duplicates entries in the sources list returned to the UI and inflates the source count.
findings.fix: Key the source id on a normalized DOI (strip ^https?://(dx.)?doi.org/ and ^doi: prefixes, lowercase) so equivalent forms collapse to one row.

findings.issue: One source uses plain http:// (http://www.simpsonassociatesinc.com/runningmath1.htm), which a browser opening from an https PWA marks insecure; the host also serves https.

A product-page URL labels a different edition than its title: URL '...essentials-of-strength-training-and-conditioning-4th-edition' with title 'Essentials of Strength Training and Conditioning (3rd ed.)' (2008). Similar product/promo pages used elsewhere (planetfitness.com/gyms/facilities, trainingpeaks blog, humankinetics product pages). Titles are all present, so this is a label match problem, not a broken link.
findings.fix: Point at the primary work (DOI/PubMed/PMC) or, if a commercial page is intentional, ensure the URL and title describe the same edition.

findings.issue: Verification: the described symptom (bare DOIs rendering as broken relative links) is already mitigated at the single render path. sourceHref() returns https://doi.org/<doi> for bare DOIs and returns undefined for anything else, and line 147 only wraps a value in <a> when sourceHref() is truthy. So today no broken link is produced; the risk is confined to the stored data and non-UI consumers.
findings.fix: Move normalization upstream (src-001) so the DB is canonical; keep this guard as defence-in-depth. Optionally extend sourceHref() to also handle 'ISBN <digits>' -> openlibrary.

findings.issue: Wrong/mismatched-DOI check cleared for the sample: 31 distinct bare DOIs resolved on Crossref with HTTP 200 and matching title/journal. Newest entries resolve too (10.3389/fspor.2026.1806303, 10.7717/peerj.21806, 10.1123/ijspp.2025-0578, all 2026-dated and found). Only cosmetic unmatched cases are wording/capitalisation variants of the same paper sharing one DOI (12 DOIs map to >1 title string) and one online-first year (10.1080/17461391.2020.1773934 is 2021 in the JSON, 2020 in Crossref). No fabricated or cross-paper DOIs found in the sample.
findings.fix: No action; optionally standardise citation titles and use the print year.

findings.issue: Missing metadata check: 0 of 529 claims are missing citation.year and 0 are missing citation.venue (both present, including for the ISBN entries).

summary: 27 wave JSON files, 529 claims. doi_or_url is not normalized: 249 (47%, 183 distinct papers) are bare DOIs (start '10.'), 275 are absolute URLs (218 doi.org, 57 non-doi.org), and 5 are ISBN strings. The consolidation script stores the raw string, so the column is non-canonical; worse, the source id is keyed on that raw string, so 21 papers cited as both '10.x' and 'https://doi.org/10.x' create duplicate research_sources rows. The described broken-relative-link symptom is already prevented in the only UI renderer (SessionDetail.svelte sourceHref()), so no link is broken today; the real defect is data-level and affects any new consumer/export. Fix at the source: in consolidate-research.ts normalize `10.\d{4,9}/...` to https://doi.org/<doi> (reusing it for the dedup key), canonicalize ISBNs to openlibrary, upgrade the one http:// URL, and fix the 3rd/4th-edition label mismatch. 31-DOI sample all resolved and matched titles; no wrong DOIs found; year/venue present everywhere.
